source.title: $\textit{Revelio}$: Interpreting and leveraging semantic information in diffusion models
source.authors: Dahye Kim; Xavier Thomas; Deepti Ghadiyaram

record.tranche_reason: The study uses k-sparse autoencoders as an interpretability tool to extract visual features, but does not test superposition, feature interference, capacity competition, or the claim versions as scoped.
record.gate_note: The study measures semantic label-purity of k-SAE features in diffusion models. These results concern a related representation-learning setting, not the specified LLM claims or superposition geometry. Diff-C classification scores and cited findings are not rows because they do not measure the claimed feature properties.
record.test_reason: The study trains k-SAEs on diffusion-model activations (SD 1.5, SD 2.1, DiT) as an interpretability tool. Its only k-SAE metric is σlabel, the class-label spread of top-activating images. It never compares SAE features against raw neurons, and it measures no feature overlap or interference, capacity allocation, SAE completeness, stability or canonicality, or feature dimensionality. The subjects are vision diffusion models, not LLMs. The results therefore bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that k-SAEs are an effective tool for dissecting diffusion models, and that visual abstraction oscillates from coarse to fine and back to coarse with depth. They also find that representation granularity depends on architecture, pre-training data and timestep, and that light-weight Diff-C classifiers on diffusion features transfer well, competing with CLIP.
record.recipe_differences: No reproduction of the Toy Models of Superposition method; the study trains k-SAEs on diffusion-model activations and measures visual-label purity.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported feature purity varies with dataset, layer, timestep, diffusion architecture, and input resolution.

fits_no_version.finding: In diffusion models, the label purity (σlabel) of k-SAE features varies with layer, dataset granularity, timestep, model (SD 1.5 vs 2.1) and architecture (U-Net vs DiT). For example, up ft1 is purest on Oxford-IIIT Pet and bottleneck is purest on Caltech-101.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The semantic granularity of SAE features in diffusion models depends on layer, timestep and dataset granularity.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The study does not directly measure feature overlap, interference, capacity pressure, importance-dependent allocation, or feature dimensionality. Its purity measure uses dataset class labels and does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
record.rows_left_out: No retained k-SAE label-purity results were left out. Diff-C downstream classification and visual-reasoning scores were omitted because they do not measure the feature properties in the claim.

untested.parts: Toy-model geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, near-orthogonal overlapping directions.
Capacity competition and importance-dependent allocation of dimensions.
Spread of features across neurons in LLMs, or an SAE-versus-neuron comparison. The study claims monosemantic k-SAE features in diffusion models but gives no neuron baseline.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The paper asserts 'monosemantic' k-SAE features only qualitatively, with no neuron baseline, so it cannot count as a V4 test even if V4 were broadened to vision models. Text-stated timestep set {25,...,400,500} differs from Table 2b (0,25,100,200,300,500); the rows follow the table.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Neuron capacity competition, dedication of dimensions, and sharing by less-important features.
Polysemanticity in neurons and whether it arises without capacity pressure.
The study concerns diffusion models, not LLMs; it does not measure LLM features spread across neurons or SAE recovery in LLMs.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features as the model's units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
